comparator.sourceNotes: The current Leiden and LUMC programme pages confirm the three-year Medicine bachelor and its continuing structure: first-year cellular, molecular, organ-system, academic and professional foundations with patient contact; second-year disease mechanisms and clinically integrated problem blocks; and third-year faculty choice space, clinically oriented problem blocks, clinical skills and longitudinal academic and professional formation. The latest complete target-specific official table accounts for 60 EC in each year. Year 3 begins with 15 EC of genuine faculty elective space, preserved without inventing a choice. The bachelor endpoint is assessed through the CAT project, internal-medicine and neurological examinations, and the selected half-minor report rather than a separately credited thesis course. The programme has no formal route or specialisation requiring selection.

exception.reason: Leiden Medicine is an integrated medical-professional bachelor whose defining formation combines cellular and organ-system science with disease mechanisms, clinically oriented patient problems, pharmacology, longitudinal medical progress testing, patient communication, professional behaviour, care-stage and early-practice contact, clinical reasoning, history taking and physical examination. UCR offers a strong biomedical, behavioural and public-health curriculum, but no supervised patient-care placement, clinical examination and history-taking sequence, integrated diagnostic-reasoning progression, longitudinal medical-professional assessment or comprehensive clinically organized organ-system curriculum. A 24-course UCR programme could provide excellent preparation in biomedical and health sciences, but it would not be a defensible Medicine comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The latest complete official programme table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 integrates normal cellular, molecular and organ-system structure and function with a care internship, academic/scientific training, communication and professional skills, ethics, law, prevention, health promotion, technology and the medical progress test. Year 2 advances through disease mechanisms, pharmacology and integrated clinical-problem blocks supported by longitudinal academic and professional formation. Year 3 preserves 15 EC of genuine faculty elective space and combines reproduction, mental health and hormones, ageing and emergency-care problem blocks with clinical skills, early practice contacts, academic critical appraisal and the progress test. The bachelor endpoint is distributed across assessed clinical and research outputs rather than isolated as one separately credited thesis.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide substantial biomedical foundations. HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease add advanced biomedical content; HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior and the cognition and psychology sequences cover neural, behavioural and mental-health perspectives; HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology and quantitative research courses add population, behavioural and evidence perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no supervised clinical placement or patient-care course, no patient interviewing and physical-examination sequence, no longitudinal clinical-skills assessment, no integrated diagnostic-reasoning curriculum, no medicine-wide progress testing, and no comprehensive clinical-problem progression across organ systems and life stages. The available biomedical courses therefore support a biomedical-science alternative, not the profession-defining academic and clinical formation of Medicine.
